factual_methodology.summary: Primary 2022 Brazilian electoral returns, dated Datafolha polling, 2026 Brazilian longitudinal experimental study, 30-country observational survey and 2026 US Pew study checked; perceptions, feelings, electoral votes and party evaluations explicitly distinguished.

source_integrity.summary: Bilingual manuscripts include 19 direct scholarly, institutional and original-publication references across 11 distinct source hosts. Classical theorists are presented as conceptual frameworks, not contemporaneous empirical measurements.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: As-of 2026-11-10 cutoff stated, with explicitly dated observations from 2022, 2024, 2025 and 2026. Election 2022 compared with 2026 perception polls without mistaking them for contemporaneous measures.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Eleven coherent analytical sections connect historical theory, affective identity, economic and cultural insecurity, political incentives, platform experiments, institutional legitimacy, and falsifiable rival interpretations without political endorsements.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two numeric charts in each language reproduce TSE 2022 shares and Datafolha 2026 perceived climate; two Markdown evidence tables, one causal flow and one comparative regional map per language; both chart numerical signatures exactly match.

research_depth.summary: Both language editions substantially exceed the 1700-word floor, contain 11 substantive sections, 19 citations and cover social, political, psychological, institutional and economic mechanisms.

evidence_traceability.summary: Prominent numerical claims traced to named original TSE, Datafolha, OECD, Pew and Nature studies; dates and populations stated; findings from observational and experimental designs kept separate.

counterfactual_review.summary: Tests specify how corrected misperception, similar economic circumstances, and feed-ranking interventions could fail to change hostility; alternative material, cultural, institutional, and media explanations contrasted.

translation_equivalence.summary: Full EN/PT-BR research narratives follow parallel argument and citations; tables, diagram and map are semantically parallel; the two charts include identical underlying numeric values.

political_neutrality.summary: No advocacy or electoral ranking. Distinguishes criticism, criminal wrongdoing, peaceful protest and the individual liability of violent participants; refuses to equate all voters with actors in institutional attacks.

contrary_evidence: Reducing exposure to like-minded sources on Facebook did not detectably reduce polarization in a 2023 experiment.
The 2018 exposure-to-opponents field experiment shows confrontational contact may increase disagreement.
2026 X algorithm findings distinguish changes in specific policy attitudes from nonsignificant polarization changes.
limitations: Datafolha 2026 reports perceived division, not a direct census of interpersonal hostility.
Cross-country associations between reported hostility, democracy and inequality are observational and survey instruments vary.
Classical philosophical works are conceptual frameworks, not comparable empirical estimates.
Platform experiments measure specific users and interventions over limited horizons, not guaranteed real-world effects.
notes: Independent QA stage performed against the final three Git blobs and controlled v2 pending contract. Primary sources and journal articles sample-checked against source claims. Local npm command execution unavailable through GitHub connector; all accessible structural, source and bilingual checks manually verified.

publication.research_question: Why do political differences become interpersonal hatred and how are social identity, economic insecurity, institutions and media systems transmitted into affective polarization?
assumptions_and_limits: Datafolha 2026 measures perceived polarization rather than direct personal hostility.
The 2022 electoral vote margin does not measure affective polarization.
US and Brazilian polls have different questions and samples and are not merged into a common index.
Classical theories inform mechanisms but are not 2026 quantitative evidence.
Platform experiments differ in treatment, duration and outcomes.
counterfactuals: Polarization may persist without a major economic shock.
Reducing exposure to like-minded posts need not reduce measured polarization.
Perceived hostility may exceed actual policy disagreement.
publication.source_integrity: Direct links to TSE, MPF, OECD, Pew, peer-reviewed papers and dated Datafolha reports; observational claims distinguished from experiments.

producer_checks.content_depth: EN/PT-BR both exceed 4,000 approximate raw words and 3,700+ substantive words
